findings.detail: Offline-delete resurrection. removeItem/removeItemWithCloud delete locally and attempt the cloud call, but on failure only set _syncError without recording a pending-delete. Since the item stays in the cloud and is not in _pendingSync, the next pullFromCloud pulls it back (it is in cloudById and not overlaid), so an offline delete silently reverts. This is asymmetric with the upsert path, which does track pending ids. It sits at the edge of the acceptance criteria (which emphasize never dropping offline-created items), so it does not block the stated goal, but it is a real offline correctness bug.
findings.fix: Add a persisted pending-delete set (mirror the __pending__ pattern), add the id on a failed/offline delete, replay the delete on the next sync, and subtract those ids from the pull merge until the cloud confirms removal.

findings.detail: Unrelated changes bundled in the same commit range as the task: ~1584 insertions across assets/translations/pt-BR.json, four lib/ui/* screens (machine_status_card, config_file_details_page, files_page, imprint_view), cloud_sync_button.dart, and arquitetura.md. Only the cold-start retry in cloud_sync_button is loosely adjacent; the rest are out of scope and make the inventory change harder to review in isolation.
findings.fix: Move the translation and lib/ui/* changes into a separate commit/PR so the shared-cloud-inventory change stands alone.

findings.detail: pullFromCloud treats the cloud as authoritative for any id not in _pendingSync, so a local edit that pushed successfully (and thus left the pending set) and was later changed on another device will lose on the next pull. This is the intended last-write-wins v1 rule, but it is undocumented as a product decision and worth an explicit confirmation.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment confirming last-write-wins is the accepted v1 conflict policy, or confirm with the owner that losing a locally-synced-then-remotely-edited value is acceptable.

summary: The task goal is fully met and verification is green. Backend: /api/supply is now one shared global inventory keyed on SHARED_SCOPE="__shared__" with a per-item non-destructive upsert on /sync (the old per-device bulk delete is removed so an empty payload deletes nothing), GET returns the whole shared set, DELETE is by item_id across the shared scope, the HTTP contract shape is unchanged, no schema migration is introduced, and src/, alembic/, and the sibling backend/ project are untouched; py_compile passes (exit 0) and FEAT-001's uvicorn smoke test evidence (cross-device visibility, empty-sync retention, upsert-in-place, shared delete, 404) is consistent with the code. Client: SupplyHub is offline-first with a Hive box 'supply_hub_items' loaded on construction, every mutation persisted locally, push failures tracked via a persisted pending-sync set instead of a silent catch, a non-destructive merge-by-item_id pull that overlays pending local items so offline-created items are never dropped, the misleading comment corrected, and a persisted stable device_id plus cold-start retry; flutter analyze lib/features/supply_hub reports no issues and all 7 unit tests pass (confirmed here). Approving with three non-blocking findings: a real but narrow offline-delete resurrection gap (failed deletes are not tracked as pending, so a deleted item reappears on the next pull), an out-of-scope bundle of translation/UI changes that should be split out, and an undocumented last-write-wins conflict policy worth an explicit note.
